conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I’m okay, just dealing with some memories that creep up on me sometimes. They can make me feel like I’m back in that moment again.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: When those memories come up, how do they affect your feelings or thoughts in the moment?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: When the memories surface, it feels like a heavy weight pressing down. I start to think that something bad is going to happen again, and it’s hard to shake that feeling off. It can be overwhelming, like I’m trapped in that past moment.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: Has anything in your environment recently triggered those memories or feelings for you?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Yeah, just the other day I heard a loud noise outside that snapped me right back to a time when I felt really vulnerable. It sent me into a state of alarm, and I couldn't focus on anything else for a while.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: How did you manage to cope or respond to that feeling of alarm once it surfaced?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I didn't really do much to cope. I just sat there feeling the anxiety build up, trying to convince myself it wasn't happening again. It felt pointless, but I didn’t know what else to do.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: In that moment, what thoughts were running through your mind while you tried to convince yourself it wasn't happening again?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I kept thinking that I should be safe now and that this noise had nothing to do with my past. But then, doubt crept in—what if it was a sign that danger was around the corner? It was hard to trust that things were different.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: Did you notice any physical sensations in your body during that time of doubt and anxiety?
